_comment: Composite indexes Firestore cannot infer on its own.
Kept here rather than only clicking the link in the error, for the same
reason firestore.rules lives in this repo: a console-only change exists
in exactly one project and is invisible to anyone reading the code. A
query that needs an index fails with FAILED_PRECONDITION until it is
deployed — `firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes`.
Note that being correct in git is not the same as being deployed. The
clan feature already shipped once with rules that were right here and
absent from the live project, and every write silently permission-denied.
The card game lobby's recent-matches list:
where('players', arrayContains: uid).orderBy('createdAt', desc)
`players` is a plain list, so array-contains finds a player's own
matches without any extra field, and the read rule on this
collection already restricts results to matches they were in.
"Kembali ke Pertandingan" resumable-match lookup
(BattleRepository.findResumableMatch):
where('players', arrayContains: uid)
.where('status', '==', 'active')
.orderBy('createdAt', desc)
Deliberately separate from the plain recent-matches index just
above — that one has no status filter and backs the history
list, which correctly wants every match regardless of status.
This one exists so a resumable match is found directly by
status instead of hoping it still sits inside history's
most-recent-N window, which is exactly the bug this replaced
(a genuinely open match could age out of a last-5 slice once
5 newer matches of any kind existed).
NOT YET DEPLOYED — same standing rule as every other index in
this file: being correct here is not the same as being live;
deploying needs `firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes` as
a separate, explicit action this change deliberately does not
take.
RISK-3 subscription backstop's daily near-expiry sweep
(functions/subscription_backstop.js, findNearExpiryCandidates):
where('subscription.tier', '==', 'premium')
.where('subscription.expiresAt', '<=', now + 3 days)
An equality filter plus a range filter on a DIFFERENT field needs
a composite index even though each field alone is auto-indexed.
The weekly long-tail sweep (findAllPremiumCandidates) uses only
the single equality filter and needs no index of its own — this
one entry covers both.
Weekly Global Ranking payout query (functions/award_top_coins.js,
awardTopGlobalCoinsOnce): ranks a closed period's participants by
points desc, then attempts desc, then uid (document id) asc — the
approved deterministic tie-break.
collectionGroup is 'users' because this targets the SUBCOLLECTION
globalScorePeriods/{periodId}/users — NOT the unrelated root-level
users/{uid} collection, which has its own separate index entry
above for a completely different query shape. Firestore indexes a
collection by its ID regardless of nesting depth, so the same
name here is coincidental, not a conflict — composite indexes are
additive per exact field-set, not exclusive per collection ID.
queryScope is COLLECTION (one specific period's own subcollection
under one known parent document), not COLLECTION_GROUP — the
payout only ever ranks one already-identified period at a time,
never queries across every period's users at once.
The trailing __name__ field must be listed explicitly, not left
to Firestore's automatic implicit tiebreak: the query orders
__name__ ASCENDING while the immediately preceding field
(attempts) orders DESCENDING — a different direction than the
last explicit field, which Firestore does not infer on its own.
NOT YET DEPLOYED as of this implementation (see
TEISOU_ROADMAP_MASTER.md's Weekly Global Ranking section) —
deploying requires `firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes`,
a separate, explicit action this implementation deliberately
does not take.
